reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 35. Nay or No: 5. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 40 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 210 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Recommit — RED Tape Act (H R 6398)
roll_calls.plain_language: H.R. 6398 (RED Tape Act) removes the requirement under the Clean Air Act that the Environmental Protection Agency review and comment on newly authorized federal construction projects and other major federal agency actions that already require review under the National Environmental Policy Act and proposed federal regulations. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

roll_calls.question: On Passage — RED Tape Act (H R 6398)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill removes the requirement under the Clean Air Act that the Environmental Protection Agency review and comment on newly authorized federal construction projects and other major federal agency actions that already require review under the National Environmental Policy Act and proposed federal regulations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.
